excluded_test_iterations.reason: Initial capped fixture held server slots through a final sleep after its body had already completed. Spurious refusals made both variants wait for the original, so this does not isolate the scheduling defect.

Corrected final-write capacity release, but the first ordering assertion included single-chunk tail hedges. Both passed. The final regression checks the first later multi-chunk group, failing the preserved old executable and passing the fix.

limitations: The initial three-helper trial and doubling policy remain experimental. The original valid stream is preserved. Cancelled group leases return unfinished work; terminal helper failures disarm the lease to avoid blind retries.
All 75 timed files across the two stages verify. Latest 51-file cohort has median desktop/adaptive C 4.117/4.245, D 6.065/6.761 and B 1.334/1.259 seconds. The adaptive policy still loses C and D.
Latest public adaptive/zero/curl medians: Rust 1.654/1.343/1.438, Node .779/.739/.778, Python 1.036/1.116/1.137. Rust and Node losses are retained; network variation remains material.
Three repetitions cover all positions for three-tool cohorts and both positions for two-tool cohorts. They do not eliminate network variation or pair independently random D faults.
C is an explicitly scaled 32 MiB exploration. B and D are standard sizes. Downloaded publisher artifacts are never executed.
64 real-wire expected outcomes pass on the actual x64/x86 binaries; 68 example tests pass per architecture, seven external cases ignored each. Latest clippy passes both architectures.
